intro.title: Auth Context
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a React authentication context to manage user login state across your app. You'll learn how to use React's Context API to create a centralized provider that shares authentication data, like a user object or login status, with any component. The main technologies involved are React's createContext, useContext hook, and useState for state management. By the end, you'll have a working auth context that can be used to conditionally render content based on whether a user is logged in.
intro.usecase: Auth Context is essential for managing user authentication state across entire React applications, similar to how platforms like Netflix or Spotify maintain your login status across all pages. In e-commerce sites like Amazon, it controls access to checkout flows and personal dashboards while keeping user data secure. Developers implement this pattern in admin panels, banking apps, and social media platforms to conditionally render protected routes, user menus, and permission-based UI elements. This centralized approach prevents prop drilling and ensures consistent authentication logic throughout complex applications.
